name: Shape Familiarity and Preference for Curvature in Object Drawings
description: Faithful replication of Experiment 1 in Chuquichambi, Palumbo, Rey & Munar (2021), "Shape familiarity modulates preference for curvature in drawings of common-use objects", PeerJ 9:e11772. Task 1, liking: 88 black-and-white drawings of everyday objects (watch, teapot, lamp, chair, phone…) appear one at a time in random order. Each object has a curved and a sharp-angled version, hand- or computer-made, shaded or not. Participants rate each drawing on a 0–100 slider from "I don't like it" to "I like it very much". Task 2, familiarity selection: each object pair is shown side by side, with left/right position randomised. Participants choose the drawing whose shape is the most familiar for that object, or "Both equally familiar" (coded 1 curved, 2 equal, 3 sharp, as in the authors' data). Analysis as in the paper: linear mixed models of liking with contour × familiarity selection (and category, shading, view), with random effects for participant and stimulus. Stimuli: the exact drawings used in the paper (file list from the authors' OSF data, osf.io/xgj69), taken from the IUAV image database (Bertamini & Sinico 2019, osf.io/cx62j, CC BY-NC 4.0). Credit: doi:10.7717/peerj.11772. For non-commercial research; removed if the authors object. Differences from the original study: (1) 44 of the 45 pairs; the electric-guitar pair (027a2/027s2) is not in the public IUAV dataset. (2) The 8 practice trials are omitted, because the paper does not list which 4 extra pairs were used. (3) Online instead of OpenSesame in a lab. The slider must be clicked or moved before continuing, and the response time is recorded. (4) The individual-difference questionnaires (Art interest/knowledge, NEO-FFI Openness, HEXACO Unconventionality, Types of Intuition Scale) are not included; only age and gender are asked. (5) Experiment 2 (two-alternative forced choice with approach/avoidance animation) is not part of this template.
author: Chuquichambi, Palumbo, Rey & Munar

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part voluntarily and know I can stop at any time.

elements.name: liking_rating
elements.title: Liking ratings of curved and sharp-angled object drawings
elements.description: 88 drawings of common-use objects from the IUAV image database (44 pairs: a curved and a sharp-angled version of the same object; hand- or computer-made; shaded or not). Random order; each drawing stays until the participant clicks the 0–100 slider ('I don't like it' to 'I like it very much'). Value: {liking (0–100), rt_ms}. Trial metadata (object, contour, shading, category) is in the trials list. Analysis as in the paper: linear mixed models of liking with contour × familiarity selection, random effects for participant and stimulus.

elements.name: familiarity_selection
elements.title: Familiarity selection: which shape of the object is more familiar?
elements.description: Each of the 44 pairs is shown side by side (left/right position randomised, order randomised). The participant selects the shape that is most familiar for that object, or 'Both equally familiar'. Value: {selection: 1 = curved familiar, 2 = equally familiar, 3 = sharp familiar (the paper's coding), curved_side: 'left'|'right'}.

<style>
:root{--bg:#eceee8;--card:#fff;--ink:#22261f;--muted:#5f675a;--accent:#2d6a6a;--accent-ink:#fff;--line:#d9ddd2;--warn:#b3261e;--miss:#fdecea}
*{box-sizing:border-box}html,body{margin:0;background:var(--bg);color:var(--ink);font:16px/1.5 system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",Roboto,sans-serif}
main{max-width:820px;margin:0 auto;padding:20px 16px 40px}
h1{font-size:1.3rem;margin:0 0 10px}
p{margin:0 0 12px;color:var(--muted)}
.card{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:14px;padding:16px;margin-top:14px}
.btn{appearance:none;border:0;border-radius:10px;padding:12px 20px;font:inherit;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;background:var(--accent);color:var(--accent-ink)}
.btn:disabled{opacity:.4;cursor:not-allowed}
.q{margin-top:18px}.q>b{display:block;margin-bottom:4px}
label.opt{display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:center;padding:8px 12px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:10px;margin-top:6px;cursor:pointer;background:var(--card)}
.top{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;margin-bottom:8px}
.t{color:var(--muted);font-size:.9rem}
.bar{height:5px;background:var(--line);border-radius:3px;overflow:hidden;flex:1;margin-left:12px;max-width:260px}.bar>i{display:block;height:100%;background:var(--accent)}
.pic{background:#e3e6df;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden}.pic img{width:100%;max-height:min(50vh,460px);object-fit:contain;display:block}
.it{padding:10px 6px;border-top:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:8px}
.it .x{font-weight:500;margin-bottom:6px}
.sc{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(7,1fr);gap:2px}.stim{background:#fff;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;display:flex;justify-content:center}.stim img{width:min(100%,60vh,520px);height:auto;display:block}input.tx{font:inherit;padding:8px 10px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:8px;width:100%;max-width:200px}
.sc label{display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;font-size:.85rem;color:var(--muted);cursor:pointer;padding:2px 0}
.sc input{width:20px;height:20px;margin:0 0 2px}
.ends{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:.78rem;color:var(--muted);margin-top:2px}
.it.miss{background:var(--miss)}
.err{color:var(--warn);margin-top:8px;min-height:1.2em}
.credit{max-width:820px;margin:0 auto;padding:0 16px 24px;font-size:.78rem;color:var(--muted)}
</style>
<style>
.sl{margin-top:16px}.sl input[type=range]{width:100%;accent-color:var(--accent)}.sl.untouched input[type=range]{opacity:.45}
.pair{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:10px}.pair .stim img{width:100%}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<main id="app" aria-live="polite"><p>Loading…</p></main>
<footer class="credit">Drawings: IUAV image database (Bertamini & Sinico 2019; IUAV University of Venice students), osf.io/cx62j, CC BY-NC 4.0; selection as in Chuquichambi, Palumbo, Rey & Munar (2021), PeerJ 9:e11772, doi:10.7717/peerj.11772. Used with credit for non-commercial research; removed if the authors object.</footer>
<script>
(function(){
  var KEY='objcurve2021:';
  var app=document.getElementById('app'), Q={}, E={}, M={}, ans={}, done={liking_rating:{},familiarity_selection:{}};
  function esc(s){return String(s==null?'':s).replace(/[&<>"]/g,function(c){return {'&':'&','<':'<','>':'>','"':'"'}[c];});}
  function err(m){var e=app.querySelector('.err');if(e){e.textContent=m||'';e.style.visibility='visible';}}
  function hideErr(){var e=app.querySelector('.err');if(e)e.style.visibility='hidden';}
  function ok(r){return !(r&&r.ok===false);}
  function load(k){try{return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY+k));}catch(e){return null;}}
  function save(k,v){try{localStorage.setItem(KEY+k,JSON.stringify(v));}catch(e){}}
  function q(n){return Q[n]||{};}
  function page(html,btn,cb){app.innerHTML=html+'<div style="margin-top:18px"><button class="btn" id="go">'+esc(btn)+'</button></div><div class="err"></div>';document.getElementById('go').onclick=cb;
    app.onchange=function(e){hideErr();var r=e.target.closest&&e.target.closest('.it');if(r)r.classList.remove('miss');};}
  function send(list,b,fin){b.disabled=true;Promise.all(list).then(function(rs){var bad=rs.filter(function(r){return !ok(r);})[0];if(bad){b.disabled=false;return err(bad.error);}fin();});}
  function shuffle(a){a=a.slice();for(var i=a.length-1;i>0;i--){var j=Math.floor(Math.random()*(i+1)),t=a[i];a[i]=a[j];a[j]=t;}return a;}
  function order(name){var o=load('o_'+name);var ids=E[name].trials.map(function(t){return t.id;});if(!o||o.length!==ids.length){o=shuffle(ids);save('o_'+name,o);}var by={};E[name].trials.forEach(function(t){by[t.id]=t;});return o.map(function(id){return by[id];});}
  function next(){
    window.scrollTo(0,0);
    if(!ans.intro)return intro();
    var n='liking_rating';
    if(!ans.seen_like)return instr(n);
    var tr=order(n);for(var i=0;i<tr.length;i++)if(!done[n][tr[i].id])return like(tr[i],i,tr.length);
    n='familiarity_selection';
    if(!ans.seen_fam)return instr(n);
    tr=order(n);for(i=0;i<tr.length;i++)if(!done[n][tr[i].id])return fam(tr[i],i,tr.length);
    if(!ans.about)return about();
    finish();
  }
  function intro(){
    var miss=E.liking_rating.trials.some(function(t){return !M[t.image];});
    if(miss){app.innerHTML='<h1>Pictures missing</h1><p>Media folder drawings must hold the 88 object drawings.</p>';return;}
    page('<h1>Drawings of everyday objects</h1><p>You will see drawings of common-use objects. First you rate how much you like each drawing. Then you see two drawings of the same object side by side and choose which shape looks more familiar for that object.</p><p>It takes about 15 minutes. Your answers are anonymous and used only for research.</p><div class="card"><label class="opt" style="margin-top:0"><input type="checkbox" id="ok"> '+esc(q('consent').title)+'</label></div>','Start',function(){
      if(!document.getElementById('ok').checked)return err('Please confirm to continue.');
      send([SPSite.answer('consent',true)],this,function(){ans.intro=true;save('a',ans);next();});});
  }
  function instr(n){
    var like=n==='liking_rating';
    page('<h1>'+(like?'Task 1 of 2':'Task 2 of 2')+'</h1><div class="card"><p style="color:var(--ink)">'+(like?'A drawing will be presented at the centre of the screen. Indicate how much you like the drawing by clicking on the horizontal sliding bar, from "I don’t like it" to "I like it very much". There are '+E[n].trials.length+' drawings.':'Two drawings of the same object will be presented, one on the left and one on the right. Choose the drawing whose shape is the most familiar for that object, or choose "Both equally familiar". There are '+E[n].trials.length+' pairs.')+'</p></div>','Continue',function(){ans[like?'seen_like':'seen_fam']=true;save('a',ans);next();});
  }
  function bar(i,N,w){return '<div class="top"><span class="t">'+w+' '+(i+1)+' of '+N+'</span><div class="bar"><i style="width:'+(100*i/N)+'%"></i></div></div>';}
  function like(t,i,N){
    var f=M[t.image],t0=Date.now(),touched=false;
    page(bar(i,N,'Drawing')+'<div class="stim"><img alt="Drawing of a '+esc(t.object)+'" src="'+esc(f.url)+'"></div><div class="sl untouched it" data-k="liking"><input type="range" min="0" max="100" step="1" value="50" id="sl" aria-label="How much do you like this drawing? 0 = I don’t like it, 100 = I like it very much"><div class="ends"><span>I don’t like it</span><span>I like it very much</span></div></div>','Next',function(){
      if(!touched){app.querySelector('.sl').classList.add('miss');return err('Please click on the bar to give your rating.');}
      var v={liking:Number(document.getElementById('sl').value),rt_ms:Date.now()-t0};
      send([SPSite.answer('liking_rating',v,{key:t.id,shown:[f.name]})],this,function(){done.liking_rating[t.id]=true;next();});});
    var s=document.getElementById('sl');var mark=function(){touched=true;s.parentNode.classList.remove('untouched');s.parentNode.classList.remove('miss');hideErr();};
    s.addEventListener('input',mark);s.addEventListener('pointerdown',mark);s.addEventListener('keydown',mark);
  }
  function fam(t,i,N){
    var side=load('side_'+t.id);if(side!=='left'&&side!=='right'){side=Math.random()<.5?'left':'right';save('side_'+t.id,side);}
    var L=M[side==='left'?t.curved:t.sharp],R=M[side==='left'?t.sharp:t.curved];
    page(bar(i,N,'Pair')+'<div class="pair"><div class="stim"><img alt="Left drawing of a '+esc(t.object)+'" src="'+esc(L.url)+'"></div><div class="stim"><img alt="Right drawing of a '+esc(t.object)+'" src="'+esc(R.url)+'"></div></div><div class="card it" data-k="fam"><b>Which shape is the most familiar for this object?</b>'+[['left','The left one'],['equal','Both equally familiar'],['right','The right one']].map(function(o){return '<label class="opt"><input type="radio" name="fam" value="'+o[0]+'"> '+o[1]+'</label>';}).join('')+'</div>','Next',function(){
      var x=app.querySelector('input[name=fam]:checked');if(!x){app.querySelector('.it').classList.add('miss');return err('Please choose one answer.');}
      var sel=x.value==='equal'?2:((x.value===side)?1:3);
      send([SPSite.answer('familiarity_selection',{selection:sel,curved_side:side},{key:t.id,shown:[L.name,R.name]})],this,function(){done.familiarity_selection[t.id]=true;next();});});
  }
  function about(){
    var c=q('gender');
    page('<h1>About you</h1><div class="card"><div class="q it" data-k="age" style="margin-top:0"><b>'+esc(q('age').title)+'</b><input class="tx" id="f_age" type="number" inputmode="numeric" min="16" max="99"></div><div class="q it" data-k="gender"><b>'+esc(c.title)+'</b>'+(c.choices||[]).map(function(o){return '<label class="opt"><input type="radio" name="gender" value="'+esc(o.value)+'"> '+esc(o.text)+'</label>';}).join('')+'</div></div>','Finish',function(){
      var miss=[],a=Number(document.getElementById('f_age').value),g=app.querySelector('input[name=gender]:checked');
      if(!(a>=16&&a<=99))miss.push(app.querySelector('.it[data-k=age]'));if(!g)miss.push(app.querySelector('.it[data-k=gender]'));
      if(miss.length){miss.forEach(function(r){r.classList.add('miss');});return err('Please answer the questions marked in red (age 16–99).');}
      send([SPSite.answer('age',a),SPSite.answer('gender',Number(g.value))],this,function(){ans.about=true;save('a',ans);next();});});
  }
  function finish(){
    app.innerHTML='<h1>Thank you!</h1><div class="card"><p>In the original study, 49 students at the University of the Balearic Islands liked the curved drawings more than the sharp-angled ones. This preference was stronger when the curved shape was judged the more familiar one, and disappeared when the sharp-angled shape was judged more familiar.</p><p style="font-size:.82rem">Method: Chuquichambi, E. G., Palumbo, L., Rey, C., & Munar, E. (2021). Shape familiarity modulates preference for curvature in drawings of common-use objects. PeerJ 9:e11772, doi:10.7717/peerj.11772. Drawings: IUAV image database (Bertamini & Sinico 2019).</p><p id="fin">Submitting…</p><div class="err"></div></div>';
    SPSite.complete().then(function(r){if(!ok(r)){err(r.error||'Some answers are missing.');var m=r.missing||[];setTimeout(function(){m.forEach(function(x){if(x==='consent')ans.intro=false;else if(done[x])done[x]={};else ans.about=false;});save('a',ans);next();},1800);}
      else{var s=document.getElementById('fin');if(s)s.textContent='Your answers have been saved. You can close this window now.';}});
  }
  SPSite.onReady(function(ctx){
    var SPEC;try{SPEC=JSON.parse(document.getElementById('sp-scheme').textContent).survey;}catch(e){SPEC={pages:[]};}
    SPEC.pages.forEach(function(p){p.elements.forEach(function(e){var g=SPSite.getQuestion(e.name)||{};E[e.name]=e;Q[e.name]={title:g.title||e.title,choices:(g.choices&&g.choices.length)?g.choices:e.choices};});});
    (SPSite.getMedia('drawings')||[]).forEach(function(f){M[f.name]=f;});
    var a=(ctx&&ctx.answers)||{};ans=load('a')||{};
    ['liking_rating','familiarity_selection'].forEach(function(n){((a[n]&&a[n].trials)||[]).forEach(function(t){if(t.key)done[n][t.key]=true;});});
    ans.intro=a.consent===true;ans.about=a.gender!=null;
    next();
  });
})();
</script>

config.description: Faithful replication of Experiment 1 in Chuquichambi, Palumbo, Rey & Munar (2021), PeerJ 9:e11772: liking ratings of curved and sharp-angled drawings of common-use objects, then a familiarity selection task for each object pair.

paper.title: Shape familiarity modulates preference for curvature in drawings of common-use objects
